    <title>End-to-End Graph-Sequential Representation Learning for Accurate Recommendations</title>
    <updated>2024-03-15T00:40:50Z</updated>
    <link href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.00895v3" rel="alternate" type="text/html"/>
    <link href="https://arxiv.org/pdf/2403.00895v3" rel="related" type="application/pdf" title="pdf"/>
    <summary>Recent recommender system advancements have focused on developing sequence-based and graph-based approaches. Both approaches proved useful in modeling intricate relationships within behavioral data, leading to promising outcomes in personalized ranking and next-item recommendation tasks while maintaining good scalability. However, they capture very different signals from data. While the former approach represents users directly through ordered interactions with recent items, the latter aims to capture indirect dependencies across the interactions graph. This paper presents a novel multi-representational learning framework exploiting these two paradigms' synergies.
